title: Past forty
translation: Someone past forty who still has a love life and keeps it quiet: well, what can you do. But when they talk about it openly and joke about sex and other people's affairs, it doesn't suit their age, and it's embarrassing to watch.

Things that are generally hard to listen to and embarrassing to watch: an old man who joins the young people and keeps talking so they'll think he's fun. A nobody who talks about some well-known person as if they were close friends. A poor household that loves throwing parties and puts on a big show for its guests.
original: {四十|よそぢ}にも{余|あま}りぬる{人|ひと}の、{色|いろ}めきたる{方|かた}、{自|おのづか}ら{忍|しの}びてあらむは{如何|いか}はせむ、
{言|こと}にうち{出|い}でて、{男女|をとこをんな}のこと、{人|ひと}の{上|うへ}をもいひ{戯|たは}るるこそ、{似|に}げなく{見|み}ぐるしけれ。
{大|おほ}かた{聞|き}きにくく{見|み}ぐるしき{事|こと}、{老人|おいびと}の{若|わか}き{人|ひと}にまじはりて{興|きよう}あらむと{物|もの}いひ{居|ゐ}たる、{数|かず}ならぬ{身|み}にて、{世|よ}のおぼえある{人|ひと}を{隔|へだ}てなきさまにいひたる、{貧|まづ}しきところに{酒宴|しゆえん}このみ、{客人|まらうど}に{饗応|きやうおう}せむときらめきたる。
literal: That a person who is over forty keeps his amorous side hidden, as it happens: what can be done about that;
but to bring it out in words and talk and joke about matters of men and women and about other people's affairs: that is unbecoming and unsightly.

Things that are generally unpleasant to hear and unsightly: an old person who mixes with young people and keeps talking to be entertaining; a person who does not count talking about a person of high reputation as if there were no distance between them; in a poor place, liking banquets and making a dazzling show to entertain guests.

notes.text: {四十|よそぢ}: forty, with the native counting word ぢ for decades of life. Forty was already old age: in section 7, Kenkō says it would be best to die before forty.
'What can one do about it?' That is, it can't be helped, and it is not worth complaining about. The complaint is about talking, not about the love life.

notes.quote: 似げなく見ぐるしけれ
notes.text: こそ … けれ: the realis form closes the こそ. {似|に}げなし: 'not fitting', here 'not fitting one's age'.
'A person who does not count', a nobody. People often used the phrase about themselves, out of modesty.
'As if there were no distance', as if they were on familiar terms. Name-dropping.
きらめく: 'to glitter', here 'to make a dazzling show'. The list ends on this item with no closing comment.
